audit.whatIsWrong: Five of the seven level-chart rows contradict their own why text. whys[0] says Gnar wins level 1 'outright' but win[0] is Skill; whys[2] describes the hook landing and punishing you but win[2] is Gnar; whys[4] calls level 6 'your single biggest swing' but win[4] is Skill; whys[5] says he walks you down and roams but win[5] is Gnar; whys[6] says 'neither of you closes the 1v1' but win[6] is Gnar.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Gnar, Gnar, Nautilus, Skill, Gnar, Nautilus, Skill] and matches the prose on every row.
audit.corrected: Whole chart flipped as one atomic group in both layers; ratings realigned (Gnar rows 6-7/10, Nautilus rows 4/10, Skill rows 5/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer phases were generic template text — 'Stridebreaker is your spike', 'trade around Dredge Line's cooldown' — that named no real timing and did not match the content layer's much better spike story.
audit.why: The actual spikes in this lane are level 2 (Hyper third-hit proc before Riptide exists), level 3 (his hook online), level 6 with Mega banked, and level 6 without it. Dredge Line's real cooldown is 14s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].why rewritten to the content layer's story with the 14s hook cooldown stated at level 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Titan's Wrath (W) is never mentioned anywhere in this matchup's text. It is a 12-second shield that eats exactly the burst Mega Gnar is trying to land, and while it holds his attacks deal damage over time to you and everything around you.
audit.why: Riot's W text plus the _missing shield-absorbs-burst rule for this matchup. Committing Mega's Wallop-into-GNAR! into a fresh Titan's Wrath wastes the one window Gnar gets.
audit.corrected: Stated in dosFull[2].d, which previously held a copy-pasted Dredge Line sentence under the title 'Boomerang-poke from range'.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] is titled 'Build MR' but its description was a verbatim copy of tradeGood and said nothing about items. report[8] also lists no MR at all while tldr and winCon both open with 'Build MR'.
audit.why: Nautilus's threat is magic damage plus a root-into-knockup chain; the entry should name the items that answer it.
audit.corrected: Description rewritten to Mercury's Treads plus Spectre's Cowl and the CC chain.

edits.before: Boomerang + hop kite wins every melee matchup early. Identify how Nautilus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Mini's ranged autos plus a Boomerang win level 1 outright — Dredge Line is his only answer, and sidestepping it leaves nothing.

edits.before: Rage management is the champion — track your own bar. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Hyper at 2 lands a third-hit proc plus Boomerang for a free chunk before Riptide exists — your strongest early window.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nautilus must walk into your range.
edits.after: One Dredge Line lands him on you, his passive roots on the next auto, and Riptide punishes any greedy step-up at 3.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: It cuts both ways: with Rage up you threaten a Wallop stun, but caught in Mini the hook chains his root onto a body with no Hop.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Bait the 14-second hook, then GNAR! him into the lane wall for a wall-stun kill — your single biggest swing in the lane.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Dredge Line's cooldown.
edits.after: Stuck in Mini his Depth Charge knockup beats your poke, and as a tank he just stacks and roams.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Nautilus carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Neither closes the 1v1 — he can't catch a careful Mini, you can't burst a tank — so your wall-GNAR! decides it.

edits.before: Boomerang Nautilus's last-hits, AA-hop out of his reach, and time Mega so the transform lands ON his engage window.
edits.after: Mercury's Treads and a Spectre's Cowl blunt Riptide chip and shrink his root-plus-knockup chain to something survivable.

edits.before: Nautilus wastes Dredge Line (Hook) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath shields on a 12s cooldown — chip it off before Mega.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first auto — break target contact fast.

notes: The content layer here was already strong and used correct ability names throughout; the damage was all in the level chart and in the full layer's untouched template text. Dredge Line also pulls Nautilus to terrain when it hits a wall, which means he can cross the lane wall your GNAR! is aiming at — I did not write that anywhere because the range/timing at which it beats a wall-stun is not something the kit file settles.
